items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 98:1
items.html: When we wish to set the worlds that are associated in the quality of mercy opposite the Partzufim of AK, in which there is no such association of the quality of mercy, we call the Sefirot Keter, Hochma, Bina, Tifferet and Malchut by the names root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall. And all the phases of AK are then reckoned in it as root, and all of Atzilut as Neshama, and all of Beria as bodies. But when we reckon the worlds by their own relations, we call them by the name Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida: Yechida is found in AK; and Haya, which is the light of Hochma, in Atzilut; and Neshama, in Beria; and Ruach, in Yetzira; and Nefesh, in Assiya. And you already know that in the relation of root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall, the worlds ABYA are lacking Yechida and Haya, as above in Item 177; and therefore there is nothing in Atzilut but Neshama. Therefore it is called here by the name Neshama, as above. (Chapter 8, Item 1)
